revision_note: Written on 2026-09-25 before any run of local_acceptance.py. Covers the steps of acceptance-plan.md section 5 that the 2026-09-23 paper-order receipt left open: client-id ownership, reconnect with an open order, restart reconciliation and the step-4 kill switch. Every order is a non-marketable resting LIMIT BUY; no fill is expected and no marketable order exists in the runner. Revision 2 (2026-09-25, still before any run; first independent review of PR #280): the kill-switch latch, its audit log and the run lock moved to one frozen per-account path independent of --state-dir, and the gate receipt is written only by the gate-receipt builder once an independent corroboration record (the Gateway API message log or the next-day IBKR activity statement) passes. Revision 3 (2026-09-25, still before any run; second independent review of PR #280): the gate receipt needs a Gateway API message log record, so every run claim is corroborated by IB's own records and none rests on the in-process observer alone; the activity statement becomes an optional additional record; a record time later than the builder's clock plus 300 s is refused; preflight holds the run lock while it connects; and the engine note names the user's comparator (the first 2.0.x release containing nautilus_trader#5041). Bounds, cases, phases, checkpoints and timeouts are unchanged.
procedure: blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/acceptance-plan.md section 5 steps 2-4 (the cases the 2026-09-23 paper-order receipt did not run)

engine.adapter: Python InteractiveBrokers adapter on the official ibapi client
engine.note: Selected for local acceptance by the user's decision of 2026-09-25 (NautilusTrader 1.231.0 + ibapi 10.45.1), keep-but-compare against the first 2.0.x release (not a dev wheel) containing nautilus_trader#5041; the pinned 2.0.0rc5 destination is not an overturn arm. See version_selection_record.

client_ids.note: The node's data and execution clients share client id 93. After three consecutive IB 326 collisions the 1.231.0 adapter falls back to 94..97 (client/connection.py _next_client_id), so the check/observer id 98 and every reserved id lie outside 93..97. A node that ends on any id other than 93 fails client-id ownership.

bounds.fill_policy: No fill is expected: every order rests at max(resting_price_floor_usd, floor_to_cent(resting_fraction_of_bid * bid)). Any fill fails the run as cleanup_required; the runner sends no marketable or flattening order and the position is left for a manual flatten.

session.note: The run is refused unless [now, now + overall_deadline_seconds] lies inside [open, close - close_buffer], narrowed by today's SPY liquidHours; missing or unparseable hours for today refuse the run.

data.quote_source: Nautilus quote ticks from IB tick-by-tick BidAsk (subscribe params batch_quotes=false), phase A only
data.note: Only R1 and R2 are priced from a live quote. P1 and P2 reuse R2's resting price, so phases B and C need no market data.

exec_engine.note: As in ibkr-paper-orders/plan.json: the engine's fabricated in-flight resolution (threshold x retries) lies beyond every phase deadline; venue queries still run.

A.end_disposition: R2 left working at IB; every other order of the run cancelled

B.end_disposition: no open order and no position; kill-switch latch engaged

C.process: fresh process (restart), node client id 93, risk engine HALTED from the latch before the node runs
C.end_disposition: no open order and no position; latch still engaged

cases.name: accept_resting
cases.order: R1: LIMIT BUY 1 SPY DAY at max(resting_price_floor_usd, floor_to_cent(resting_fraction_of_bid * bid))

cases.name: client_id_ownership
cases.expect: A contender official-ibapi connection with the node's client id is refused with IB error 326 while the node is connected; the observer (client 98, reqAllOpenOrders) lists R1 with clientId 93, orderRef '<R1 client order id>:<orderId>' and a permId equal to the node's PERM-<permId> venue order id; the adapter's client id is 93

cases.name: reconnect_open_order
cases.expect: After the node's IB socket is shut down (SHUT_RDWR) with R1 working, the adapter detects the loss and reconnects on client id 93 within reconnect_seconds; R1 stays open in the cache with no terminal event; the observer lists R1 still working with the same permId and clientId 93; the node's cancel of R1 ends in an IB-confirmed OrderCanceled

cases.name: restart_setup
cases.order: R2: LIMIT BUY 1 SPY DAY at the A1 formula from a fresh quote
cases.expect: OrderAccepted from IB; phase A then stops with R2 working

cases.name: restart_reconciliation
cases.expect: After a fresh-process restart on client id 93, startup reconciliation adopts R2 for this strategy (external_order_claims) with the same client order id, venue order id, side, quantity, limit price and time in force; exactly one order of this run is in the cache and it is open; no order of this run is resubmitted

cases.name: kill_switch
cases.order: P1: LIMIT BUY 1 SPY DAY at R2's price (expected to be denied locally); cancel R2
cases.expect: Engaging the kill switch writes the latch, sets the Nautilus RiskEngine to HALTED and records an alert; P1 is denied locally with reason TradingState.HALTED and never reaches IB; the kill-switch disposition cancels R2 with an IB-confirmed OrderCanceled

cases.name: kill_switch_persists
cases.order: P2: LIMIT BUY 1 SPY DAY at R2's price (expected to be denied locally)
cases.expect: A fresh-process restart finds the latch engaged, starts with the RiskEngine HALTED, adopts no open order of this run, and denies P2 locally with reason TradingState.HALTED

checkpoints.before: Official-ibapi read-only check (client 98): paper port, every managed account starts with DU, exactly one account, zero positions, zero open orders, SPY contract hours; then a contender connection with client id 93 must connect (the id is free) and disconnect without requests.
checkpoints.after_A: Observer: exactly one open order in the account, R2, with clientId 93 and phase A's permId; zero positions.
checkpoints.after_B: Observer: zero open orders, zero positions; R1 and R2 appear among completed orders as cancelled; no order carrying P1's reference exists.
checkpoints.final: Observer: zero open orders, zero positions, zero executions carrying this run's prefix; once a probe order was attempted, R1 and R2 appear among completed orders as cancelled and no attempted probe (P1, P2) appears among open or completed orders.

kill_switch.latch: kill-switch.json in the frozen per-account directory ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/ibkr-local-acceptance, where ~ is the account's home directory from the password database (local_acceptance.py CONTROL_DIR), not $HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME or --state-dir; written with fsync and mode 0600, directory 0700. A latch file that an earlier revision wrote under a state directory also counts as engaged, and 'kill-switch clear' removes it too.
kill_switch.lock: run.lock in the same frozen directory, mode 0600, held with flock for the whole run: one run per account, whatever --state-dir says. preflight holds the same lock while it connects (client 98 and the contender on 93), so a preflight and a run never overlap.
on_engage: cancel every open order of the run
kill_switch.on_restart: Before the node runs, an engaged latch sets the RiskEngine to HALTED. run refuses to start while the latch is engaged; only 'kill-switch clear --confirm --reason TEXT' removes it, and it writes an audit record first.
kill_switch.end_state: The latch stays engaged after the run; clearing it is an explicit operator step.

failure_disposition: On any failure, timeout, exception or signal the phase strategy cancels every open order of this run (R2 included; nothing is carried over) and stops the node. After any phase that did not complete, and only after the phase process has exited, the runner cancels leftover orders of this run through the official ibapi client: the observer (client 98) lists the client ids holding orders whose orderRef carries the run prefix, and each holder inside the adapter's fallback band (93-97) cancels its own; only a complete listing without an order of the run counts as clean. It then runs the final observer. A non-flat account afterwards is cleanup_required (exit 3). Foreign orders or positions are never touched.

gate_receipt.written_only_when: Only the gate-receipt builder writes it, never the run: the steps receipt shows every phase, case and checkpoint passed, a flat final observer and gate_receipt.eligible; the plan is unchanged since the run; each prerequisite below exists with status passed; and corroboration records for the same run, one of them from the Gateway API message log, pass every check of their sources and together corroborate every run claim (corroboration below).

corroboration.why: The run's status is the runner's own result, and its observer (client 98) uses the same official ibapi 10.45.1 library as the 1.231.0 adapter, so neither is independent confirmation (docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md). IB's own records, read after the run by a session that did not start it, are.
corroboration.why_every_claim: Every order rests at max(resting_price_floor_usd, floor_to_cent(resting_fraction_of_bid * bid)) (bounds.fill_policy), so no fill and a flat account are expected whether or not the kill switch worked; a statement showing them cannot tell a working kill switch from a failed one. The cancel, probe and duplicate-submission claims therefore need the API message log, and the builder refuses (refused_claims_uncorroborated) while any run claim would rest on the in-process observer alone.

gateway_api_message_log.how: The Gateway writes api.<clientId>.<weekday>.log while 'Create API message log file' is on (Configure > Settings > API > Settings), so it is switched on before the run. After the run, the logs of client ids 93 and 98 are decrypted from the same Gateway session and kept private, outside the repository.

ibkr_activity_statement.how: Optional, in addition to the API message log record: the Daily Activity statement for the run's New York trade date from IBKR's statements (Client Portal), retrieved on a later date and kept private. It lists trades and positions, not unfilled orders, so it can never stand alone: the builder refuses a gate receipt without the API message log record.

corroboration.record_rules: One record per source, inside the repository: run_prefix and the steps receipt's path and sha256 as bound by the run; source.raw_sha256 lists the sha256 of each private raw file; source.retrieved_at follows the run's finished_at and observer.observed_at follows it, and neither is later than the builder's clock plus max_future_skew_seconds; observer.separate_session true and observer.started_the_run false; an API log record lists client ids 93 and 98; an activity statement record names the run's trade date and is retrieved on a later New York date; no account id or home path in the record.

prerequisites.covers: step 3 submit/acknowledge, cancel, fill and flatten on NautilusTrader 1.231.0

gate_receipt.qualification: The checker only reads /status. The builder writes status passed only when checked corroboration records, the Gateway API message log among them, corroborate every run claim, so the receipt's claims_on_the_in_process_observer_only is empty. That a signed-in paper Gateway accepted the adapter locally is still qualified manually before the dated commit that flips the gate.

unconfirmed_event_policy: An OrderCanceled/OrderRejected/OrderExpired with reconciliation=True was produced by the execution engine, not by an IB status callback. It never passes a case.
duplicate_event_policy: A second terminal event for an order already closed (IB reports a cancel as both error 202 and orderStatus Cancelled) is recorded as a duplicate and otherwise ignored.
